Chemical and catalyst waste streams are individually reported. Spent reforming catalysts are assumed to carry a residual value in buyback from the supplier; however, no resale value is credited and instead, a $0/ft3 disposal cost is assumed. For cases with capture, the waste stream contaminated with triethylene glycol from CO drying is disposed of at a cost of $1.30/gal. 2 2.11.3 Financial Factors The method used to determine capital recovery factor and levelization factors for O&M and fuel costs is found in “Cost Estimation Methodology for NETL Assessment of Power Plant Performance” (NETL, 2025b), which developed financial factors for various industrial sectors based on market data. These metrics are described and defined according to the formulas in this section. 2.12.1 Cold Gas Efficiency The CGE is useful for comparing the overall system performance of ammonia production alone and is calculated as the ratio of the total thermal output of the ammonia product to the total thermal input of the fuel fed to the system, expressed as a percentage. The efficiency can be calculated on both a HHV and a LHV basis.
